text:
alice_support: Customer reporting truncated JSON when using go-sdk v0.8.4 StreamScan. Happens on long streaming responses; non-streaming Curl works. Ticket #13579.

alice_support: Excerpt from client log: 
``
2026-02-20T09:12:05Z ERR stream decode: unexpected end of JSON input
raw: "{\"id\":\"r_77\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"This is a very long message that seems to be cut off in mid\"}"
``

carol_eng: Do they have any middleware or reverse proxy? Chunking reassembly issues often surface with proxies or corporate firewalls.

alice_support: They tried behind a corp proxy and also locally w/o a proxy on macOS, go1.21. Repro attached (small server + client).

mike_sdk: Sounds like a scanner boundary bug where a JSON token gets split across Read() calls and the scanner returns ErrUnexpectedEOF instead of buffering. We shipped a reassembly + retry in v0.9.2. v0.8.4 lacks that.

mike_sdk: Quick triage list:
- Confirm HTTP uses Transfer-Encoding: chunked on the response (should be true).
- Get netcat/tcpdump of wire bytes to see where chunk boundaries are.
- Reproduce with a tiny server that intentionally splits tokens.

nate_sre: Note: we deployed a keepalive tweak last week that injects small CRLF keepalive chunks on idle streams. Some older scan code treats CRLF as terminating empty chunk. Might be the same failure mode. I'll run a rollback in staging to test.

mike_sdk: Short-term customer options while we investigate:
1) Upgrade to go-sdk v0.9.2 (recommended).
2) If can't upgrade, switch to manual decoding using bufio.Reader + json.Decoder loop to tolerate split tokens.
3) Add a small read-retry around ErrUnexpectedEOF in the stream path (non-ideal but pragmatic).

mike_sdk: Example hacky client fallback: 
``
// read loop tolerant of split tokens
r := bufio.NewReader(resp.Body)
d := json.NewDecoder(r)
for {
    var raw json.RawMessage
    if err := d.Decode(&raw); err != nil {
        if errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unexpected end of JSON input") {
            time.Sleep(25 * time.Millisecond) // wait for more bytes
            continue
        }
        log.Printf("stream fatal: %v", err)
        break
    }
    handle(raw)
}
```

alice_support: Customer tried a local repro that writes first 40 bytes then sleeps 30ms then writes rest; they hit the same error.

mike_sdk: Repro server example (emit chunk split):
``
func handler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    body := "{\"id\":\"x\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"A very long streamed message...\"}}]}"
    // write in two parts intentionally to simulate boundary
    w.Write([]byte(body[:40]))
    time.Sleep(30*time.Millisecond)
    w.Write([]byte(body[40:]))
}
```

carol_eng: If Nate's staging rollback shows repro disappearing, we should push a prod mitigation ASAP and notify affected customers.

nate_sre: Rolling keepalive CRLF rollback to staging now; will run the repro harness and report back.

mike_sdk: Internal bug filed SDK-1024 (scanner split-token resilience). Patch included in v0.9.2; added backport candidate for v0.8.x branch for customers who can't move yet.

deploy-bot: Canaries scheduled: staging rollback -> canary test 2026-02-21T01:30Z, if green then staged roll 2026-02-21T03:00Z.

alice_support: I'll update ticket #13579 with upgrade recommendation, the json.Decoder snippet, and request a tcpdump if upgrade fails. Will loop back after canary. :thumbsup:
